1Q5 f16_19:9.notes: The transcription contains damaged and uncertain characters, particularly around 'אד#נ?י?[' (Lord). The phrase 'כל זאת' is translated as 'all this' based on repeated phrase evidence. 'ידי׳נו רמה' is rendered as 'a hand raised' per dominant contextual rendering, though the support is partial (0.75). The verb 'אגור' is translated as 'dwells' based on its morphology and lexical gloss. The final punctuation mark (׃) is omitted as it has no clear translation.

1Q5 f16_19:10.en: For a people perishing of counsel, they have no understanding. If only they were wise, they would comprehend this, they would understand to their end.
1Q5 f16_19:10.notes: Positions 1-9: Phrase evidence supports 'by understanding' for positions 8-9, but the translation retains 'have no understanding' to preserve the literal sense of the glosses. Positions 11-17: The translation follows phrase evidence for 'they were wise they will comprehend' (positions 12-13) and 'they will understand (to) end' (positions 15-17), with 'this' (position 14) translated literally. The verb 'between' at position 15 is uncertain and translated as 'understand' based on gloss and phrase evidence.

1Q5 f20:1.en: To Benjamin he said Beloved of YHWH it will dwell to security on him sheltering on all the day and between his shoulders he dwelt
1Q5 f20:1.notes: The translation follows high-confidence phrase evidence for the sequences 'to security on' (positions 7-9), 'he said David' (positions 3-4), and 'on all the' (positions 11-13). The sequence 'all the day' (positions 12-14) is supported but less dominant. The name 'David' is omitted as the visible form is 'beloved' (position 4). The final verb 'he dwelt' (position 18) is retained despite potential repetition with 'it will dwell' (position 6) to preserve all recoverable material.

1Q5 f20:2.en: And to Joseph he said be blessed YHWH of the earth's present from heaven from dew and from the primeval ocean's lying beneath
1Q5 f20:2.notes: Uncertain elements include the reconstruction of 'and' at the start, the form of YHWH, the meaning of 'present', and the syntax of the final prepositional phrases.

1Q5 f20:3.en: The yield of the sun and from the present of produce of months and from the present of the earth and the fullness of the pleasure of the dweller of the blackberry bush, her yield to the head
1Q5 f20:3.notes: The translation includes reconstructed text for 'yield' and 'fullness'. The term 'Jerah' is translated as 'months' based on the plural form. The phrase 'her yield' refers to the earth's yield, inferred from context. The final phrase 'to the head' is uncertain due to the fragmentary nature of the text.

1Q5 f20:4.en: Joseph and to the crown of the head of the consecrated one his brothers first-born bullock ornament and horns of a wild ox his horns in people he will gore together
1Q5 f20:4.notes: Uncertain reconstruction of 'first-born bullock ornament' and 'his horns in people'. Phrase evidence supports 'crown of the head of the consecrated one' and 'horns of a wild ox'.

1Q5 f21:1.en: And to Zebulun, he said, 'Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar in your tents.' People of the mountain will call
1Q5 f21:1.notes: The transcription contains uncertain and reconstructed elements, including a damaged verb form and an uncertain gloss for Zebulun. The translation preserves the visible morphology and syntax without adding unlicensed connectors or subjects.

1Q5 f21:2.en: There they will slaughter sacrifices of righteousness, for abundance; seas will suck, and covering, hiding sand.
1Q5 f21:2.notes: The phrase 'sacrifices of righteousness' is supported by repeated evidence. The translation conservatively follows the visible morphology and lexical glosses, with uncertainty in the reconstruction of 'justice' (צֶדֶק) and the meaning of 'sea' (יָם) in this context.

1Q5 f22:1.en: The righteousness of YHWH made and his judgments with Israel. And to Dan said Dan: a lion's whelp leaps from Bashan.
1Q5 f22:1.notes: Reconstructed text in positions 1 and 11. Uncertain particle in position 10.

1Q5 f22:2.en: And to Naphtali he said, 'Naphtali is sated with pleasure, and full of the blessing of YHWH, the sea and the south he will trample down.'
1Q5 f22:2.notes: The phrase 'the blessing of YHWH' is a reconstruction based on repeated phrase evidence. The verb 'he will trample down' is an imperative in the original text, but the translation uses a future tense to maintain natural English syntax.

1Q5 f23:1.en: And to Asher, who said, 'Blessed from the sons of Asher who will be pleasing, his brothers, and he dipped in oil his foot.'
1Q5 f23:1.notes: The translation includes reconstructed text and an uncertain character (ε) at the end, which is omitted in the translation. The phrase 'he dipped in oil his foot' is a literal rendering of the visible morphology, though its meaning is unclear.
